sections.h2: How fast can a Palm Beach Gardens house sell?
sections.html:
As fast as the buyer's financing and your repair list allow. A cash buyer can close on a date you choose, while a full listing may bring a higher price at the cost of showings and inspections.

Palm Beach Gardens is a high-value market, so the tax, permit and recording details deserve more attention here than in many Florida cities. The sections below cover the city's planned origins, its numbers and the rules a seller meets.

sections.h2: How was Palm Beach Gardens built?
sections.html:
It began as a planned community. On March 20, 1959, John D. MacArthur announced plans to develop about 4,000 acres for 55,000 people, according to the city's About page.

His preferred name, Palm Beach city, was refused, so he chose Palm Beach Gardens to fit his garden city plan. He had streets and construction routed around mature trees such as the banyans, and churches went up first. By 1964 he had attracted the Professional Golfers Association, whose clubhouse opened in March 1965, and the PGA left in 1972. In 1999 the MacArthur Foundation sold about 14,000 acres, around 5,000 of them in the city.

For a seller, this history explains the mature tree cover, the waterways and the master-planned layout many buyers see on the streets.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Palm Beach Gardens?
sections.html:
Home values here sit well above most of the state, and the population skews older. The Census Bureau publishes the city-wide figures below.

sections.h2: Which city rules affect a Palm Beach Gardens seller?
sections.html:
The city's FAQ page covers several items that buyers' inspectors and title agents raise.

  • Permits: roof replacement, electrical, plumbing, mechanical work, window and door replacement and additions all need a permit, filed through the online permitting system with items such as plans, contractor details and a survey.
  • Owner-builders: homeowners may pull certain permits themselves with an Owner-Builder Affidavit but take full responsibility for the work and code compliance.
  • Trees: a Certified Arborist is on staff, tree removal falls under Section 78-328 of the city code, and a dead tree, palm or shrub should be replaced within one month.
  • Plants: Brazilian pepper, Australian pine and melaleuca are prohibited, and plant beds need three inches of mulch.
  • Violations: after notice, an owner who does not correct a violation can be sent to the Special Magistrate, with fines and liens possible.

The city also runs a Single-Family Home Improvement Grant for owner-occupied, homesteaded houses within city limits, with income capped at 120 percent of area median income and liquid assets capped at $50,000. It funds exterior hardening, energy and accessibility work such as roofs, windows and doors.

sections.h2: Does age change how a Palm Beach Gardens owner sells?
sections.html:
It can. With about a third of residents 65 or older, many sellers here are downsizing after decades in the same house, and several Florida benefits are tied to age and service.

  • An ordinance may grant owners 65 and over an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 within a household income limit. Ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser whether your address qualifies.
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount equal to their VA disability rating.
  • A tax deferral application goes to the tax collector by March 31, and a permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent of household income.
  • Homestead ends once the home is rented or stops being your permanent residence.

If you are moving within Florida, portability can carry up to $500,000 of cap savings to the new homestead, according to the statute. Amendments from chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 tax roll.

sections.h2: How do taxes and fees work when a house sells here?
sections.html:
The property appraiser values the house each January 1, and the tax collector bills in November. Unpaid bills go delinquent on April 1, and certificates are sold by June 1.

A deed in Palm Beach County carries 70 cents of documentary stamps for every $100 of price. Clerk recording charges are added, beginning at $5.00 for the first page with smaller trust fund and technology charges per page. Your title agent can total this before you accept an offer.

  • To dispute a value, file a petition within 25 days of the August notice of proposed taxes.
  • If an exemption is denied, petition the value adjustment board within 30 days of the letter's mailing.

sections.h2: What if a lender, a tax lien or an unwanted occupant is involved?
sections.html:
A judicial foreclosure sale takes place at least 20 days after final judgment and no more than 35 unless the plaintiff agrees to wait. The high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale. A homestead owner should check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale about surplus funds.

Tax certificates run on a separate track, and a holder may seek a tax deed after two years. For a person occupying a home with no right to be there, Florida lets an owner file a verified complaint with the sheriff, but false statements expose the owner to triple the fair market rent plus fees. If the person is a tenant, use the notice process instead. Check on vacant seasonal or inherited houses often.

faqs.q: Which county appraises Palm Beach Gardens homes?
faqs.a: Palm Beach County. The county property appraiser values the house and the county tax collector bills it. The city's own site links to the appraiser to verify where you live.
Its founding announcement came on March 20, 1959, when John D. MacArthur announced plans for about 4,000 acres. It is a planned community, not a historic town.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp rate here?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of price, the standard Florida rate. Only Miami-Dade differs.

faqs.q: Can a senior defer property tax?
faqs.a: Possibly. File form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31. A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the portion above 3 percent of household income.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes savings after selling?
faqs.a: Part of it, if you establish a new Florida homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one. File form DR-501T with DR-501 by March 1.
